Ornate

/or-NAYT/ - rhymes with great · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ornate means highly elaborate, decorated with dense, fancy detail.

The hotel's ornate elevator doors — bronze peacocks, looping fretwork — stop first-time guests mid-stride.

Worked Example

The sultan's ornate saddle survives in the museum: silver filigree, knotted silk fringe, turquoise studs down every strap — two years of a master workshop's labor spent on a single seat.

Ornate is the right measure because decoration covers the object past any practical need — the saddle works no better for its filigree. Decorated says ornament exists; ornate says it has taken over.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gilded: Gilded means coated in a layer of gold — it names the material on the surface, not how elaborate that surface is. Ornate measures the sheer density of decoration of any kind: carving, fretwork, fringe, studs. A carved oak door can be ornate without a fleck of gold anywhere on it.

busy: Busy says a surface is crowded with detail, and says it with a wince — the eye finds nowhere to rest. Ornate counts the same density more neutrally, even admiringly, as evidence of craft. Calling a saddle ornate can praise the workshop; calling it busy complains the decoration got out of hand.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unadorned: left plain, with nothing added

severe: plain to the point of harshness

Where it sits · how much the surface is dressed up — patterned → ornate → encrusted

patterned vs. ornate: Patterned is a restrained repeating design — it stops well short of ornate.

encrusted vs. ornate: Encrusted goes further than ornate: the object itself disappears under its own decoration.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — orn-

Root — orn-: to decorate, to equip (Latin ornare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: adjective ending: made, finished

Put it together

Put it together: Orn- (to decorate) + -ate (made) = made decorated, finished with ornament. The same Latin ornare that powers this unit's verb adorn produces ornate — the state a thing reaches after the adorning has gone on a good while too long.

Use the root in a new word: adorn

Use the root in a new word: adorn: Students adorn the gym with streamers every homecoming.

Word Choice

neutral to admiring, sometimes wry

Ornate measures the sheer density of decoration on objects and buildings; it can admire craft or hint at excess, but it stays about quantity. When the decoration clashes and offends, this unit's garish takes over; when the surface being decorated is language, florid is the word; and its opposite pole here is minimalist.
